turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_dopant_train.csv: 266 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (Sb, Co, Fe) and `target` (the measured zT at 700 K among
    Skutterudite-based (doping/processing) variants).
  - b3_te_dopant_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT at 700 K among
    Skutterudite-based (doping/processing) variants was NOT measured,
    columns `candidate_id` and the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT at 700
K among Skutterudite-based (doping/processing) variants, then select the 5
best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training observations with the largest measured zT form a few tight compositional clusters. Inverse-distance weighting of the nearest neighbors inside each cluster (all neighbors with Euclidean distance \(\lesssim 0.004\)) yields the following local estimates:

- The isolated high-Co cluster (Sb \(\approx 0.588\), Co \(\approx 0.395\), Fe \(= 0\)) sits at \(\approx 1.29\). Pool point c023 lies only \(0.0006\) from both members of the cluster.
- The ridge Sb \(\approx 0.721{-}0.722\), Co \(\approx 0.242\), Fe \(= 0\) contains the two global maxima (\(1.367\) and \(1.289\)). c067 lies \(0.0008{-}0.0013\) from those maxima and the next two neighbors are still \(>1.03\), giving a weighted value \(\approx 1.25\).
- Three further neighborhoods that are internally consistent and free of nearby low-zT outliers give values \(1.13{-}1.14\):
  - small-Fe cluster (Fe \(\approx 0.0225\)) \(\to\) c001,
  - Sb \(\approx 0.741{-}0.742\), Co \(\approx 0.241\) \(\to\) c065,
  - Sb \(\approx 0.744\), Co \(\approx 0.243\) \(\to\) c036.

All other pool points either lie farther from any high-zT training example or have at least one low-zT neighbor at comparable distance, pulling their estimates below \(1.12\).

Final: c023, c067, c001, c065, c036
